summary: Add the 5Post partner-delivery adapter and admit a separate Delivery surface for tenant credential checks while keeping unqualified shipment writes fail-closed.

impacts.evidence: The adapter validates one connector account per tenant and never accepts a caller-supplied tenant or workspace override.
API keys, JWTs and recipient data stay behind the host boundary; normalized evidence excludes raw provider payloads and PII.
No new public HTTP or OpenAPI operation is added; the existing connector-account control plane exposes only tenant setup and credential health checks.
The SDK adapter publishes no event and changes no canonical event envelope or topic.
The provider reuses the frozen Logistics SDK v1 ports and declares only capabilities supported by the partner contract.
No provider-specific table or migration is introduced; the separate Delivery surface reuses tenant-scoped connector accounts and health history.
Secret use is callback-scoped, remote access is host-mediated and shipment writes remain default-deny until live qualification.
Shipment creation and cancellation are sensitive SDK operations and remain unavailable to application callers until host policy wiring exists.
Future runtime composition must retain canonical remote references and bounded operation evidence without copying raw responses.
Create and cancel contracts carry idempotency keys and remote status is explicitly authoritative for later reconciliation.
The partner API uses host-mediated outbound calls; no guessed callback or arbitrary provider egress is admitted by this adapter.
Manifest timeout, concurrency and retry metadata bound the credential probe, while separate-surface status prevents false shipment availability claims.
The separate-surface entry can be disabled by runtime support metadata and no migration or destructive rollback is required.
Deterministic operation tests and machine-readable reports cover both carrier SDK boundaries without production credentials or network access.
